newsitem.title: USA: Emerging market debt prices mixed in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Emerging market debt prices mixed in quiet trade.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices were mixed Tuesday in quiet trade as market participants kept to the sidelines awaiting the release of U.S. producer price index due out Wednesday, some market sources said.

"People are waiting for the PPI number which is going to confirm hopefully for the market that no tightening is in the cards soon, and as long as that number is benign we should have a nice pop," said one trader, who noted that the market is also looking for direction from U.S. Treasuries.
Mexico was the star performer of the day, with its par bonds rising 1/2 to 73-5/8 bid.
One source attributed gains in Mexico to one large purchaser of the country's par bonds.
Other Mexican debt instruments also posted strong gains with the country's discs 1/2 higher at 85-3/8 and its UMS-26 3/8 firmer at 104-7/8 bid.

Meanwhile, Bulgarian debt fell on profit-taking after posting sharp gains in recent days on expectations of a currency board but traders said they expect the country's debt will continue to move higher.
"Bulgaria took profits but we believe that it will continue to trade higher," said another trader at a major U.S. investment firm.
Bulgaria FLRB were 1/2 lower at 40-1/4 and its IABs were 5/8 weaker at 52-7/8.

Elsewhere, sources said Russian Vnesh loans rose initially on news that the IMF mission had recommended that it should meet with Russia on Friday on whether to pay out delayed loan tranches to Russia but they said concerns over the budget caused prices to pare gains.

"Initially, it was taken as good news...but then people started to get a little more concerned about the budget discussion and the local market started to take a hit so as a result prices in Vnesh and Min Fins came off a bit," one said.
Even still, Russian Min Fin 3 were 3/8 higher at 83-7/8 bid and Vnesh dollar loans were unchanged at 77-7/8.
